# Section heading

A level-1 heading (`#`) renders as a full "section divider" slide in reveal.js
-- useful for the same kind of part-break you already use in PS1-3.

## A slide with math

The dynamic programming recursion for the finite-horizon cost-to-go:

$$
\costtogo_k(\state) = \min_{\action \in U(\state)} \; g_k(\state,\action) + \costtogo_{k+1}\big(f_k(\state,\action)\big)
$$

using the macros already defined in `styles/macros.tex` (`\costtogo`, `\state`,
`\action`) so notation stays consistent across all 14 lectures.

## A slide with a live code plot

Code blocks execute when the deck is rendered, so a figure like this is
generated fresh every time rather than being a static export pasted in from
MATLAB/Keynote:

```{python}
#| echo: false
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

x = np.linspace(0, 10, 200)
plt.figure(figsize=(6, 3.2))
plt.plot(x, np.sin(x), label="example signal")
plt.xlabel("t"); plt.ylabel("x(t)"); plt.legend()
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

from `Code/`), reference it like any Markdown image:
